option.title: Fully autonomous RAN alarm remediation
option.description: Closed-loop auto-remediation of RAN alarms: the SON engine resets cells on its own, with no human approval.

option.title: Supervised closed loop for the packet core
option.description: Remediation is proposed by the orchestrator; the NOC operator gives a human approval in the ITSM before execution.

option.title: On-call engineers fix routers over SSH
option.description: During incidents, engineers apply a hotfix in production directly on the routers (ssh into production).

option.title: Router configurations managed with GitOps
option.description: Intended configurations and fallback plans are versioned in Git; each change goes through a merge request and a validation pipeline.

option.title: Restoration tooling inside the core cluster
option.description: The remediation platform runs on a shared cluster with production core network functions and shares storage with production.

option.title: Independent remediation platform
option.description: The remediation platform lives in a dedicated cluster, reachable out-of-band, with a documented break-glass procedure.

option.title: Self-hosted NOC copilot
option.description: A self-hosted LLM copilot summarises alarms. It is read-only and advisory: operators act through the approved workflow.

option.title: Dispatch summaries through a public LLM API
option.description: Incident call transcripts of the MCX dispatch are summarised by a public LLM API hosted by a US provider.

option.title: AI agent applies core configuration
option.description: An AI agent with write access automatically applies configuration changes on the mobile core.

option.title: Self-healing MCPTT servers
option.description: Self-healing of MCPTT application servers: failed nodes are restarted and re-provisioned without human validation.

option.title: Vendor playbooks deployed as delivered
option.description: Fault management playbooks written by the vendor are copied to the automation server; they are not versioned.

option.title: Signalling firewall rules as code
option.description: Signalling firewall rules are maintained as code in a Git repository and deployed with GitOps.

option.title: Slice orchestrator next to the slices
option.description: The automation platform that heals slices runs on a shared cluster with production slice workloads.

option.title: Correlation rules edited in the GUI
option.description: Alarm correlation rules are edited by hand in the OSS GUI, directly in production, by the NOC team.

option.title: Energy-saving closed loop with approval
option.description: The energy-saving closed loop first runs in shadow mode, then each action is gated by a manual approval.

option.title: Kubernetes auto-remediation operators
option.description: Kubernetes operators perform automated remediation of failed nodes: drain, reimage and rejoin, as fully autonomous remediation.

option.title: Virtualization manager on the managed cluster
option.description: The virtualization management platform is co-located with the managed services on the same hosts and datastores.

option.title: PaaS delivered through GitOps
option.description: All platform manifests and automation code are versioned in Git; Argo CD applies them after pull request review.

option.title: Manual BIOS and firmware settings
option.description: BIOS and firmware settings are changed manually on each server in production by the data centre team.

option.title: Portal chatbot on a SaaS LLM
option.description: The internal developer portal chatbot sends user questions and platform logs to a SaaS LLM.

option.title: On-premise advisory assistant
option.description: An on-premise, self-hosted LLM runs on GPU nodes; the ops assistant is read-only and only provides suggestions.

option.title: Independent restore platform
option.description: The backup and restore management platform runs in a separate failure domain with break-glass access.

option.title: Terraform applied from laptops
option.description: Terraform automation code lives on engineers' laptops and is applied to production without review.

option.title: AIOps agent changes the virtualization layer
option.description: An AIOps agent executes changes in production on the virtualization layer as soon as it detects drift.

option.title: Upgrade remediation behind change approval
option.description: Failed upgrades trigger automated remediation, executed only after change approval in the ITSM.

option.title: Monitoring stack on the monitored hosts
option.description: The monitoring and management platform is deployed on the production hosts it supervises, without out-of-band access.

option.title: Ansible playbooks in GitLab
option.description: Ansible playbooks are versioned in GitLab and promoted through merge requests and a validation pipeline.

option.title: Copilot with production write access
option.description: Platform engineers use a coding copilot that holds write access to the production clusters and applies fixes.

option.title: Log summarisation by a third-party model
option.description: Production logs are sent to a third-party model API for summarisation and anomaly explanation.

option.title: Unattended disk-full remediation
option.description: Disk-full incidents on bare-metal servers trigger unattended remediation at night, without human approval.
